timeline.title: A Short History of Getting the Job
items: Leonardo da Vinci wrote a letter to the Duke of Milan listing everything he could do. It is often called the first CV.
Newspapers began printing job adverts, and the hunt for the perfect job went public.
Henry Ford gave his factory workers a five day week, helping make the two day weekend normal.
The first job websites appeared, and applying for work moved from the post box to the inbox.
today: Not in the history books yet. But definitely in the company newsletter.

letters.title: What the World Has Said About Success
items: Choose a job you love, and you will never have to work a day in your life.
Opportunities multiply as they are seized.
Pleasure in the job puts perfection in the work.
Hard work beats talent when talent doesn't work hard.
letters.hand: Good advice, all of it. Ours is simpler: you have got this, {who}.

facts.title: The Science of a Great Day at Work
items: Studies have found that happier people tend to be more productive at work.
People who feel appreciated at work are more likely to stay and do their best.
A good night's sleep helps the brain solve problems. Bedtime is a business strategy.
Having plants nearby has been linked to people feeling calmer and more focused at work.
A short walk can boost creative thinking. Meetings on foot count.
Gentle music can help some people focus. Others need total silence. Both are allowed.
facts.hand: Science can explain a lot. It cannot explain how {who} gets so much done.
